items.title: If it looks like a DDoS attack
items.summary:
In five days, three pillars of American life stopped working. On Thursday, Nov. 12, Microsoft Outlook went down worldwide, drawing more than 43,000 problem reports from 72 countries by the next morning in an outage that ran past 12 hours. On Friday, the FAA halted every departure in the country for more than four hours after its communications network failed; nearly 12,000 flights were canceled and the backlog was still felt days later. On Monday, customers of Chase, Bank of America , Wells Fargo , U.S. Bank and Truist found themselves locked out of online banking, with Chase alone drawing more than 5,000 outage reports by early afternoon.

Each organization was quick to say what it was not: an attack.

Microsoft: “ There is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity .” Chase: “ This is a technical issue, not cyber related .” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a “ nefarious attack ” on the FAA.

But look at what each one describes. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, “ Our switches, our routers, actually got overloaded with data ,” after a newly installed router fired roughly 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. A flood of requests overwhelming network equipment until legitimate traffic cannot get through is not merely similar to a denial-of-service attack. It is the textbook definition of one. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford has said that explanation does not fully account for the root cause. Microsoft has blamed a network upgrade but has not published a full post-incident report. Chase…
items.t: If it looks like a DDoS attack

items.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella: Jensen Huang ‘a singular person,’ but it’s up to Nvidia to decide whether to bring him back as CEO
items.summary:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised ousted Nvidia founder Jensen Huang as “a singular person” who has contributed immensely to the tech industry, but stopped short of calling for his reinstatement to the top job.

“I just want to give him space for what he needs to do there, and it’s not up to me. It’s up to the Nvidia board to decide what happens next,” Nadella said Tuesday at a media roundtable in San Francisco during Microsoft’s Ignite conference.

Huang, who turned Nvidia into the dominant maker of AI chips, stepped down as CEO last week of the company he cofounded 33 years ago, amid revelations of multiple affairs, including one with an executive whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy. On Tuesday, Huang broke his silence and said he would be open to returning to the CEO job. 

Nadella, who said he had exchanged text messages with Huang over the weekend, said that Nvidia has a deep bench of talent.

“I think Nvidia does have a lot of human capital and very capable leadership,” Nadella said, noting that interim CEO Colette Kress once worked at Microsoft. “I’m making sure that we have the same type of partnership, and we’re scaling Rubins as we speak,” Nadella said, referring to Nvidia’s new Vera Rubin line of processors. “It’s a pretty critical project for us.”

As one of the world’s largest cloud computing providers, Microsoft is a major purchaser of Nvidia chips, and the two companies have a longstanding relationship. Nadella appeared with Huang last month at a Microsoft Windows event.

This story is developing. Check back for updates. 

This…
items.t: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella: Jensen Huang ‘a singular person,’ but it’s up to Nvidia to decide whether to bring him back as CEO

items.title: Creator Deja Foxx says 2028 presidential hopefuls are already lining up for influencers like her and James Dumoulin

Deja Foxx thinks the next presidential race will be fought in creators’ interview chairs.

Foxx, a political creator and host of Courier’s Candid , spoke Monday at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit alongside James Dumoulin, the 24-year-old cofounder of the business interview channel, the School of Hard Knocks . When asked by Fortune Editorial Director Kristin Stoller what the two see in store for traditional media as compared to the creator economy, the two said it’s all about relationship building.

“My predictions are that creators are going to take up the lion’s share of our interview space with many of these candidates,” Foxx said. She said she has already seen it at two conferences in Washington and Denver over the past two weeks. 

“Presidential hopefuls line up for creators to come speak to them,” she said.

Stoller opened with Pew Research Center data showing that 21% of U.S. adults regularly get news from news influencers on social media, a share that rises to 38% among those ages 18 to 29. She asked whether the two see themselves as journalists.

“I think definitely to some degree,” Dumoulin said. “Traditional media is great at building audiences, but I think creators and influencers, if you want to call it, are great at actually building relationships.” Viewers who watch a creator regularly see “the successes and the failures,” he said, which makes them more likely to trust that person. 

Foxx’s first viral video was about 10 years ago, when, at 16, she confronted her senator over his vote to defund Planned Parenthood, where she had gotten care while…

When you’re in the nicotine business, responsibility needs to be at the heart of everything you do.”

items.title: To appoint the next comptroller general of the United States, follow the law
items.summary:
The new approach being employed to appoint the next Comptroller General of the United States should raise a red flag. The Government Accountability Office (GAO), which is headed by the Comptroller General, plays an important role in helping Congress discharge its responsibilities under Article I of the U.S. Constitution, particularly in connection with oversight of the Executive Branch.

We were shocked to learn that U.S. Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY), Chairman of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs (HSGAC), recently and spontaneously requested that names be submitted to him, under a short time constraint, to be recommended to the President for nomination as the next Comptroller General of the United States.

Under the GAO Act of 1980, a 10-member statutory bipartisan and bicameral Comptroller General Selection Commission was created. Chairman Paul is a member, since he is Chair of the HSGAC, but he is not the Chairman of the Commission. That Commission is required to jointly develop and transmit a list of at least three qualified nominees to the President. That is the law, and that is how the process of appointing the Comptroller General has been conducted since 1980.

The current vacancy for Comptroller General of the United States began on Dec. 30, 2025, and yet the Commission and its members have never met.

Equally shocking is that Sen. Paul took the liberty as HSGAC Chairman to insert an empty placeholder for an unnamed nominee for Comptroller General of the United States for a Nov. 19, 2026, Committee confirmation hearing.

Again, Sen. Paul…
items.t: To appoint the next comptroller general of the United States, follow the law

items.title: ‘I’m not afraid of Chinese cars’: GM’s president says Detroit will be the bastion of American manufacturing as China breaks auto export records
items.summary:
General Motors President Mark Reuss wanted to make one thing clear at the F500 Innovation Forum in Detroit: “I’m not afraid of Chinese cars.” At the same time, he said GM is taking China’s growing automotive manufacturing industry “very seriously.” China exported more than 8 million passenger vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, and Reuss’ answer is to point to Detroit’s GM’s factories.

Reuss spoke during a panel discussion with Fortune ’s Executive Editor Lee Clifford. “I think we do a lot of things really well,” he said. “Core things like safety, durability, reliability, long term, and of course design—aesthetic design.”

And the stakes are American jobs: the motor vehicles and component parts sector employed about 2.6 million U.S. workers in 2025, according to the Department of Energy , a drop of more than 50,000 from the year before. But he pointed to GM’s factories, production scale and workforce as competitive advantages that Chinese competitors can’t replicate.

“I think Detroit is doing a lot of things well,” he said. “We look at our factories and our scale, and we do scale well.”

He also pointed to GM’s people. “I think our talent is second to none. I really do,” Reuss said. “We have the best talent in this country in automotive, I believe.”

And one of the ways they were doing it? He said the company had been operating in China since 1984—studying its competitor: “We know Chinese cars,” Reuss said.

And GM still takes apart rivals’ cars from around the world to see what competitors are doing, Reuss said. “Only the paranoid survive, right?”

China is turning…
items.t: ‘I’m not afraid of Chinese cars’: GM’s president says Detroit will be the bastion of American manufacturing as China breaks auto export records

items.title: SBA chief defends policy barring green-card holders from loans, even if they can serve in U.S. military
items.summary:
Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler said Tuesday it’s “completely not true” that her agency’s new loan rules restrict immigrants. The rules she was defending bar green-card holders, who can legally work, pay taxes and, if otherwise eligible, enlist in the U.S. military, from SBA-backed loans.

Under a policy that took effect March 1 , businesses must be wholly owned by U.S. citizens or nationals to qualify for SBA-backed loans, cutting out lawful permanent residents, commonly known as green-card holders, who were previously eligible. In fiscal 2025, the agency approved 3,358 loans to businesses partly owned by lawful permanent residents, about 4% of its 85,000 loan approvals, according to the SBA . Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, Loeffler cast the rule as a question of who goes first: “Foreign nationals cannot get an SBA loan ahead of an American citizen.”

“It strikes me as odd that we can send somebody to a battlefield on behalf of the United States,” Fortune Brainstorm Editorial Director Andrew Nusca told Loeffler. “We can take their taxes, but we can’t extend to them a loan.”

“We have not yet run into a case where we’ve had to reject a veteran for that purpose,” Loeffler said. She didn’t directly address why green-card holders who serve in the military should be excluded. Instead, she pointed to the agency’s work supporting veterans, including a policy waiving down payments for eligible veteran entrepreneurs.

Loeffler also argued that the SBA has limited funding and accounts for only a small share of the broader small-business…
items.t: SBA chief defends policy barring green-card holders from loans, even if they can serve in U.S. military

items.title: ‘What if the input isn’t the news? What if the input is you?’ Bill Gross gave away 1.2 million AI business ideas for free—the Fortune 500 is next
items.summary:
A month ago, Idealab founder Bill Gross gave away 1.2 million AI-generated business ideas for free. Now he wants Fortune 500 companies to pay $250,000 a year to run the same system on their own patents.

“What if the input isn’t the news? What if the input is you?” Gross told executives at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit on Monday, in a session sponsored by Idealab.ai. He meant their patents, trade secrets and “all the things that you’ve shelved inside of your company.” Idealab plans to license the full system to companies at $250,000 a year, he said, and is offering five companies a one-year pilot for $25,000.

The pitch is aimed at a real problem: big companies hold a lot of patents that never become products. Large firms’ patents are tied to new product launches “far less so” than smaller firms’, according to research from Kellogg’s Sara Moreira and economists at Yale and the Atlanta Fed, which matched about 1.4 million products to patents. Moreira’s explanation complicates Gross’s pitch, though: big companies often use patents as a “defensive tool” to block competitors rather than to launch anything. Some of that shelved R&D is on the shelf on purpose.

The Caltech test 

Gross launched Idealab.ai in October after feeding an AI system news stories going back to 2000, every patent since 1980, product recalls, and complaints on Reddit and X, along with his own 31 methods for coming up with business ideas. He said it came back with 1.2 million ideas after about a month and roughly $1 million in AI costs, and that 131,000 people in 202 countries have searched…
items.t: ‘What if the input isn’t the news? What if the input is you?’ Bill Gross gave away 1.2 million AI business ideas for free—the Fortune 500 is next

items.title: Days after Microsoft and the FAA went dark, Chase and Wells Fargo customers can’t get to their money
items.summary:
If you had trouble logging into your bank’s website on Monday, you’re not alone. JPMorgan Chase customers spent much of the day unable to log in or move money, with the bank saying the outage spread from it’s website and app to some branches and to outside apps that connect to Chase accounts. Wells Fargo , Capital One, and Zelle also had problems with their online banking platforms as customers reported trouble.

Reports started Monday morning and climbed quickly. Downdetector logged nearly 4,500 Chase reports shortly after 1:30 p.m., most of them about website logins. By 2:22 p.m., the count had passed 20,000.

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson told Fortune . “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”

Customers described a wider disruption than that statement suggests. Comments on Downdetector mentioned problems with ATMs and in-person systems as well as online banking and Zelle. Some customers opening the Chase app got a message reading , “Some services aren’t available.”

Ashley Lutz 

The problems also reached apps outside the bank. Plaid, which links bank accounts to payment, investing and budgeting apps, said its own network was working normally but that it was seeing connection problems with Chase accounts. Customers trying to link or refresh a Chase account through another app may have gotten errors as a result.

items.title: Anthropic recognises the risks to humanity – but is its governance really up to the job? | Nils Pratley
items.summary:
The Claude AI developer’s unique setup is supposedly high-minded, but still represents extraordinary power concentration

Boardroom governance matters, even in the world of big tech, it turns out. The business of how companies are run, investors are discovering, can be more complicated than handing the founder or superstar chief executive as much control as he wants (it’s usually a he) and waiting for brilliant returns to appear. Sometimes a few checks on power are useful, especially when a crisis strikes.

This revelation is no revelation at all, of course. For about 30 years until the first generation of big US tech companies came along, the thrust of corporate governance thinking was to insist on the basic fairness of the principle of “one share, one vote”. The owners should be able to chuck out misbehaving or underperforming managers by a simple majority, in other words.

items.t: Anthropic recognises the risks to humanity – but is its governance really up to the job?
